title: Gilbert Young takes him to the Hummingbird Cabaret
summary: Trumpeter Gilbert Young took him to the Hummingbird Cabaret in 1927; he mentions his Catholic upbringing and seeing the Baby Dolls.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Tell us about your first job when you started in the...

Well, I mean, as I say, I was working and working, and I mean, it looked like I was just the unhappiest guy in town. And one day a friend of mine come off a show. He was a youngster like myself. Him and I were good friends. And incidentally, he's the guy that is the cause of me being a musician today. Gilbert Young, a trumpet player. I mean, he came to town. He came to see me, and he asked me would I come out with him that night. He wanted to go to a place to see some fellow around some business, so he brought me to a place called the Humminbird Cabaret. Well, I had never been in a cabaret in my life before. All I did was went to church and stayed around home, and the cabaret, if they'd have thought I went in a cabaret, they'd allow me to scalp me like an Indian, you know?
Were you raised as a Catholic?
Oh, yeah, yeah. I was an altar boy at St. Catherine Church.

I was on Tulane across from the charity hospital. Yeah, I was baptized and confirmed by Father Cuddy. Uh-huh. And so, well, anyhow, Gilbert took me out in this place. It was in the year 1927 on the St. Joseph night. And I walked in there, and I had never seen nothing like that. They had a group in there called the Baby Dolls. They had a stocking full of $100 bills, and I was a perfect square. I never saw nothing like that in my life. And I just added up. And from that night on, I ain't never went back home.
